clue.text: Banker has met disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A bank employee has run into some catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a bank employee, but in crosswords it can be something with banks: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so crossword setters call a river a banker; this is London's great river.

clue.text: Bootleg liquor not initially causing a fuss

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is to be dropped from the liquor word

parts.note: hooch is slang for illicit or bootleg spirits

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Illegal moonshine stirs up trouble at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially causing' means remove the first letter of 'causing' (C) from HOOCH, leaving HOOH; add A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal word for a commotion or noisy fuss over something.

clue.text: People in a graceless state

parts.note: mortals means human beings, people as opposed to gods

explanation.surface: Humans living without divine favour.
explanation.walkthrough: In Catholic teaching a grave sin cuts the soul off from sanctifying grace, hence 'graceless state'.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic doctrine holds that a grave wrong leaves the sinner without sanctifying grace until confession.

clue.text: Work hard on article that's used in campaign

parts.note: to slog is to toil away at something
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Grafting away at a piece written for an election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchphrase or motto is the thing repeated throughout a political or advertising campaign.

clue.text: Politician's protest about one crossing floor?

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is simply a politician

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
c (circa) is the abbreviation for about
a rat is a politician who deserts their party, crossing the floor of the House

explanation.surface: A politician's protest concerns someone defecting to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossing the floor in Parliament means switching party, and such a turncoat is called a RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Democratic Party is a politician of that party.

clue.text: Puzzling over death, missed clue leading to killer

indicators.note: puzzling over something means working it round in the head, signalling the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver frets about a death, a missed clue pointing to the murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a detective story; 'killer' is a tree disease, not a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal disease has killed many millions of elm trees across Europe and North America.

clue.text: Streaky lines spoil ostentatious accessories

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
bling is slang for flashy jewellery and accessories

explanation.surface: Streaks ruin some showy jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbling is a pattern of streaks or veins like those seen in marble or meat.

clue.text: Metallic sound of family grand

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A clashing noise made by a well-off family.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing noise made when metal strikes metal.

clue.text: I will support a former country, and not as part of Turkey

indicators.note: in a down clue the word placed underneath supports the one above it

parts.note: Siam is the former name of Thailand
nor means and not

explanation.surface: Someone vows to back an old nation, while refusing to treat it as Turkish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'I will support' puts I below A SIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anatolian peninsula, the Asian part of modern Turkey, was historically known by this name.

clue.text: Roofer puts newly-designed canopy on one

indicators.note: something newly designed is put together in a fresh way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder fits a freshly designed canopy on top of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the bed itself, which has a canopy over it.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of bed has a post at each corner, often supporting a canopy or tester.

clue.text: Very keen to see a short film

indicators.note: short says the word is cut back, losing its final letters

parts.note: a video is a recorded film

explanation.surface: Eager to catch a brief movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, very keen on something.

clue.text: Holding a party, get money for water-container

indicators.note: holding means the money word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to cash a cheque is to get money for it
Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Throwing a party, one raises funds for a water bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd hollowed out was traditionally used as a vessel for carrying water.

clue.text: Bean needs stick, in general

indicators.note: in places the stick word inside the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
gum is something that sticks, and to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Beans have to be staked, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'generally', but it puts one piece inside General LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans, peas and lentils belong to the legume family of pod-bearing plants.

clue.text: It grows in three seconds

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
S is the abbreviation for second
S again for second, the third of the three

explanation.surface: Something that shoots up very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'seconds' are MO (a short time) and S twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This small green plant grows over stones, trees and lawns, a vague but fair definition.

clue.text: Having company over, eat hard cooked solids

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards
cooked suggests the letters are worked over into something new

explanation.surface: With guests round, someone eats tough food that has been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns CO into OC; 'cooked' rearranges EAT HARD into TAHEDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are solids with eight flat faces, like two square pyramids joined base to base.

clue.text: From extremely English place, bring down dispatch

parts.note: to land a plane or a fish is to bring it down
to send is to dispatch

explanation.surface: Sending something off from a remote corner of England.
explanation.walkthrough: This Cornish headland is the westernmost point of mainland England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cornish headland is the far south-western tip of England, hence the extreme place.

clue.text: Shelf holds one enclosure for drier

indicators.note: holds means the shelf word contains the other letters

parts.note: a sill is a shelf at the base of a window
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cage is an enclosure

explanation.surface: A shelf holds a single box intended as a drying unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Packets of this granular substance absorb moisture, so it acts as a drying agent, a desiccant.

clue.text: Bronte family to gain playwright

parts.note: to earn is to gain
George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: The literary Bronte household aims to win over a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the Brontes themselves, but a family in Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindley, Hareton and Catherine of this surname are a family in Emily Bronte's Wuthering Heights.

clue.text: Flag sort of rose

definitions.meaning: a ... rose is grafted on a tall upright stem

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a military banner and a rose trained as a small tree.

clue.text: One singing high for fun

definitions.meaning: the skylark sings as it climbs high
a bit of fun or a prank is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: The bird famed for singing on the wing shares its name with an informal word for a jape.

clue.text: Challenging lover to lose pounds

indicators.note: to lose says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a darling is a beloved, a lover
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A demanding partner wants to shed some weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like weight, but it is L, the money sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes something bold or audacious, challenging conventions.

clue.text: Turn back in military order for C-in-C

indicators.note: in places the reversed turn inside the military command

parts.note: 'shun, short for attention, is a parade-ground command

indicators.note: back means the word for turn is read backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: An about-face within the military chain of command for the top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shun!' is the clipped parade-ground form of 'Attention!'; 'back' reverses the turn word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The shogun was the hereditary commander-in-chief of the Japanese army, effectively ruler of the country.

clue.text: Energy to burst out at the start

parts.note: a gust is a sudden burst of wind

indicators.note: at the start points to the first letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Vigour to break out from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means relish or vigorous enjoyment, energy put into doing something.

clue.text: Get away to the south, grabbing a view of the Med perhaps

indicators.note: grabbing means the escape word takes the A inside it

parts.note: to escape is to get away

explanation.surface: Fleeing southward, someone takes in a Mediterranean vista.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mediterranean is a sea, so a picture of it is an example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of a sea view is a seascape, and the Mediterranean is one example of a sea.

clue.text: Two for one, in brief

definitions.meaning: two is an example of a number divisible only by itself and one
to brief someone is to prepare them with information in advance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Two for one' looks like a bargain offer; it means two is one example. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Two is the smallest such number, and the verb also means to prepare someone beforehand.

clue.text: For execution, does not reveal fateful day

indicators.note: execution here is beheading, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: hides means does not reveal

explanation.surface: A doomed man keeps secret the day he dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For execution' says HIDES loses its head, its first letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March, the day he was warned to beware.

clue.text: Earpiece an asset in court?

indicators.note: in links the asset to the court, so read as a help for a court session

parts.note: a hearing is a session of a court
an aid is a help, an asset

explanation.surface: A device for the ear proves useful in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: This small electronic device fits in the ear to amplify sound for the hard of hearing.

clue.text: Welsh town's dry grass now irritated you

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the town itself

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: irritated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: The town's hay fever is bothering you just now.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Welsh border is famous for its secondhand bookshops and literary festival.

clue.text: One adding leaf unnecessarily to lily?

definitions.text: One adding leaf unnecessarily to lily?

parts.words: One adding leaf unnecessarily to lily?
parts.note: to gild the lily is to embellish something already beautiful, here read as applying gold leaf to a flower

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies gold leaf to a surface does the job named in the idiom about over-decorating a lily.
